title: EXO: Accelerating Storage Paravirtualization with eBPF
problem: KVM/QEMU-based paravirtualization incurs multiple context switches for guest I/O requests, creating non-negligible software overhead with modern fast NVMe storage devices.
motivation: Reducing I/O path overhead is critical for applications leveraging high-performance storage in virtualized environments.
method: When a virtual machine needs to access storage, requests normally have to switch from the Linux kernel to QEMU (the virtual machine software) running in user-space, creating overhead. EXO uses eBPF, a method for running programs directly inside the Linux kernel, to create a direct path that performs guest-to-host memory address translations (converting virtual machine addresses to real computer addresses) without needing to switch to QEMU. For complex operations that need full backend processing, the system falls back to the original slower path through QEMU.
key_novelty: EXO uses eBPF (a method for running code directly in the Linux kernel) to create a fast path for virtio-blk storage requests that bypasses the user-space QEMU backend by performing guest-to-host memory address translations (converting virtual machine addresses to real computer addresses).
contributions: eBPF-based in-kernel fast path for virtio-blk storage paravirtualization avoiding context switches
Hybrid approach preserving fallback to full QEMU backend for complex operations
Performance competitive with or exceeding existing storage paravirtualization solutions

metrics.speedup: similar or higher than existing storage paravirtualization solutions

primary_theme: In-kernel eBPF fast path for storage paravirtualization
